Eggless Pumpkin Chocolate Chip Bundt Cake (with Chocolate Glaze)

ByOriana Romero Published:October 9, 2026October 9, 2026
Jump to RecipeAdd as a trusted source on Google

Instaread

This eggless pumpkin chocolate chip bundt cake is moist, warmly spiced, and packed with mini chocolate chips in every slice, finished with a thin chocolate glaze. It comes together in two bowls with a whisk, and there’s nothing to stack, frost, or decorate. One look at it on the dessert table and nobody will guess it’s egg-free.

Video Muted

Oriana’s Thoughts On The Recipe

If your family goes crazy for anything chocolate chip the way mine does, this is the fall cake for you. It’s my favorite pumpkin cake with one cup of mini chocolate chips folded in, baked in a Bundt pan, and finished with a light chocolate glaze — and honestly, the chips make it irresistible.

I wanted something fun for fall that still felt special enough for a holiday table. A Bundt cake does that all on its own: it comes out of the pan looking beautiful, so there’s no layering, no piping, and no decorating stress. You just glaze it and set it out.

After more than a decade of baking without eggs for my family, this is exactly the kind of recipe I love most — simple, reliable, and something everyone at the table can enjoy, egg allergy or not. My family loves it just like every pumpkin recipe I make (we’re a pumpkin-loving house!), and I love baking with pumpkin puree because it’s such a great egg substitute.

Do you prefer the classic pumpkin cake? Check out my The BEST Eggless Pumpkin Cake.

Why You’ll Want to Try My Recipe

  • Egg-free by design. No eggs and no egg replacers. Yogurt, applesauce, and pumpkin do the job.
  • Chocolate chips in every bite. Mini chips spread through the whole cake, so every slice has chocolate, not just the bottom.
  • Two bowls, one whisk. No mixer, no creaming butter, no special equipment beyond a Bundt pan.
  • A showstopper with zero decorating. The Bundt shape does the work. A thin chocolate glaze is all it needs.
  • Made for the fall table. It’s cozy enough for a weekend treat and pretty enough for Thanksgiving dessert.
  • Tested by a real allergy mom in a real family kitchen.

How This Cake Works Without Eggs

In most cakes, eggs add moisture, hold the crumb together, and help it rise. This cake was designed to do all of that without them. The pumpkin puree and applesauce bind the batter and keep it soft; the yogurt adds richness and moisture, and the oil keeps the crumb tender for days. Baking powder and baking soda give the lift — the baking soda reacts with the yogurt and brown sugar so the cake rises tall in the pan. No flax eggs, no egg replacer, no special ingredients.

How to Grease and Flour a Bundt Pan So the Cake Releases Cleanly

The number one worry with any Bundt cake is that it’ll stick, and the fix is all in the prep. Brush a thin layer of shortening into every groove and around the center tube — a pastry brush or a folded paper towel works best. Add a spoonful of flour, then tilt and tap the pan until every surface has a thin white coat, and tap out the extra. Hold the pan up to the light: any shiny bare spot is where the cake will grab, so touch it up before the batter goes in. Cooling matters too, so follow the cooling time in the recipe card before you flip it.


Ingredients You’ll Need, Substitutions & Notes


Scroll down to the recipe card for all the details, including measurements and instructions.

Most of these are pantry staples you already have — a few are worth a quick note.

  • Pure pumpkin puree is a must. Don’t use pumpkin pie filling — it’s already sweetened and spiced, so it throws off the whole batter.
  • Mini chocolate chips are the key to chocolate in every bite. They’re light enough to stay spread out in the thick batter, where regular chips are heavier and more likely to sink.
  • Plain yogurt or sour cream keeps the cake moist and tender and helps the baking soda give it lift. Either one works.
  • Applesauce adds moisture and helps hold the crumb together without eggs. Use unsweetened.
  • Pumpkin pie spice gives the cake its warm fall flavor. No pumpkin pie spice? You can make my Homemade Pumpkin Pie Spice Blend in a minute.

Food Allergy Notes & Swaps

This recipe does not contain eggs, tree nuts, peanuts, soy, sesame, fish, or shellfish as ingredients. Manufacturing lines change — read every label every single time, even brands you have used before. That habit has never steered me wrong.

Need Dairy-Free or Gluten-Free?

If you are navigating additional dietary needs alongside the egg-free requirement, I have detailed guides for both: How I Replace Dairy in My Egg-Free Recipes – Baking Without Eggs and Gluten

Ingredient Swap Suggestions

  • Dairy-Free: To make this recipe dairy-free, you can easily swap out the dairy ingredients for non-dairy alternatives.
    • Butter: Substitute butter with dairy-free butter substitutes. Miyoko’s Creamery Organic Vegan Butter, Trader Joe’s brand vegan butter, and Earth Balance Vegan Buttery Sticks are my favorite butter substitutes for baking. For the best flavor, use a vegan butter that tastes good. Use sticks or blocks, not tub (spreadable) butter.
    • Heavy Cream: You can use a non-dairy cream, such as Silk, Country Crock Plant Cream, or Califia Farms.
    • Sour Cream: Use your favorite dairy-free sour cream. I use and recommend Tofutti Better than Sour Cream.
    • Chocolate Chips: Use your favorite dairy-free chocolate. One of my favorites is Ghirardelli Non-Dairy Dark Chocolate Chips for Baking. Here you can find other brands I like and use.
  • Gluten-Free: Use a gluten-free, all-purpose flour blend. Look for a gluten-free flour blend specifically formulated for baking, as it will have the right combination of flours and starches to mimic the texture of wheat flour. My favorite is Better Batter Original Blend. I also like Doves Farm Freee Gluten-Free All-Purpose Flour, but this blend does not contain xanthan gum, so you need to add 1/4 teaspoon of xanthan gum per cup (140 g) of gluten-free flour blend.

Tips & Troubleshooting

  • Don’t overmix. Whisk just until no dry flour shows, then fold in the chips. Overmixing makes the cake tough.
  • Spoon, don’t dump. Spoon the thick batter into the pan and smooth the top so it bakes evenly and sits flat when you flip it.
  • Test in more than one spot. If the toothpick comes out with melted chocolate, you hit a chip, not raw batter. Try another spot. You’re looking for clean or a few moist crumbs.
  • My cake stuck to the pan. A missed spot in the greasing is the usual reason. Next time, check the pan in the light before adding the batter. If it’s holding on, run a thin spatula gently around the edges and center tube before flipping.
  • My chips sank to one side. Use mini chips and fold them in at the very end, right before the batter goes into the pan.
  • My glaze ran right off. The cake was still warm, or the glaze was too hot. Let the cake cool completely and let the glaze sit a few minutes until it coats the back of a spoon.
  • My glaze is too thick. Stir in a teaspoon of warm cream at a time until it pours.

What I Learned Testing This Recipe

The biggest lesson? Grease and flour your Bundt pan really well. One missed spot is all it takes for the cake to stick and tear, so take the extra minute to get into every groove — that’s the key to success here.

Beyond that, this is a very straightforward recipe: mix the wet ingredients, bring in the dry, fold in the chips, and you’re done. Nothing complicated. And let the cake cool completely before you glaze or slice it. While it’s still warm, it feels sticky and too moist; once it’s fully cool, the crumb sets up just right.

Variations

  • Simple sugar dusting: Skip the glaze and dust the cooled cake with confectioners’ sugar instead.
  • White chocolate chips: Swap the mini chocolate chips for mini white chocolate chips for a sweeter, cozy version.

Serving Suggestions

This cake belongs on the fall dessert table — Thanksgiving, Friendsgiving, a potluck, or a cozy weekend at home. Slice it at room temperature so the crumb is soft, and the glaze is set. It’s lovely with a cup of coffee or a mug of homemade apple cider.

Recipe Card

Eggless Pumpkin Chocolate Chip Bundt Cake

Oriana Romero
This eggless pumpkin chocolate chip bundt cake is moist and perfectly spiced, with mini chocolate chips in every bite and a thin chocolate glaze on top. It's egg-free by design, made with pantry staples in two bowls with just a whisk. No mixer, no layers, and no decorating needed.
No ratings yet
Print Recipe Pin Recipe Save Recipe Saved!
Prep Time 20 minutes mins
Cook Time 1 hour hr 10 minutes mins
Total Time 1 hour hr 30 minutes mins
Servings 12 servings

Equipment

  • Kitchen Scale
  • Mixing Bowls
  • Bundt Pan

Important

• For best results, I highly recommend using a kitchen scale to measure the ingredients.

Ingredients
 

For the Pan:

  • Shortening for greasing
  • All-purpose flour for dusting

For the Cake:

  • 3 cups (420 g) all-purpose flour
  • 3 teaspoons (12 g) baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon (6 g) baking soda
  • 1 teaspoon (4 g) kosher salt
  • 2 teaspoons (5 g) pumpkin pie spice
  • ¾ cup (170 g) unsalted butter, melted
  • 1 ½ cups (300 g) light brown sugar
  • ½ cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/3 cup (80 g) plain yogurt or sour cream
  • 1/3 cup (80 g) applesauce (unsweetened)
  • ¼ cup (60 ml) neutral-tasting oil (such as vegetable or canola oil)
  • 1 can (15 ounces / 425 g) pure pumpkin puree
  • 1 cup (190 g) mini chocolate chips

For the Chocolate Glaze:

  • ½ heaping cup (115 g) chocolate chips or chunks
  • ½ cup (120 ml) heavy cream
  • 2 teaspoons (10 ml) light corn syrup (optional)

Instructions
 

  • Prep the pan: Preheat the oven to 350ºF (180ºC) for at least 15 minutes. Grease the Bundt pan with a thin layer of shortening, getting into every groove and around the center tube. Add a spoonful of flour, tilt and tap until every surface has a thin white coat, then tap out the excess. Touch up any shiny bare spots — that's where the cake will stick.
  • Whisk the wet ingredients: In a second medium bowl, whisk together the melted butter, brown sugar, granulated sugar, yogurt, applesauce, oil, and pumpkin puree until smooth and glossy.
  • Add the dry ingredients: Add the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and pumpkin pie spice. Whisk just until smooth and no dry flour remains. The batter will be thick — that's exactly right.
  • Add chocolate chips: Fold in the mini chocolate chips with a spatula until evenly scattered. Don't keep mixing after that.
  • Fill the pan: Spoon the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top with a spatula.
  • Bake: Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until the top springs back when pressed lightly and a toothpick comes out clean or with a few moist crumbs. This is a big, moist cake, so give it the full time — don't rush it, and don't worry if it runs long. If the toothpick comes out with melted chocolate, you hit a chip — test another spot.
  • Cool: Let the cake cool in the pan for 20 minutes, then flip it onto a wire rack. Let it cool completely before glazing.
  • Make the chocolate glaze: Place the chocolate in a medium heatproof bowl. Heat the heavy cream in a small saucepan over medium heat until it barely simmers, with small bubbles around the edges (or microwave for 1 to 2 minutes). Don't let it boil. Pour the cream over the chocolate, let it sit for 2 to 3 minutes, then stir slowly until smooth and glossy. Stir in the corn syrup, if using.
  • Glaze the cake: Let the glaze cool for a few minutes until it coats the back of a spoon. Spoon a thin layer over the top of the cooled cake, letting a few drips run down the sides. Let it set before slicing. Any leftover glaze is lovely spooned over slices when you serve.
Oriana’s Notes
 
Storage: Cover the cake and store it at room temperature for up to 2 days, or in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. 
 
Freezing: Freeze the baked cake for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and bring to room temperature before serving. 
 
Food Allergy Note: This recipe contains no eggs, tree nuts, peanuts, soy, sesame, fish, or shellfish as ingredients. Manufacturing lines change, so read every label every time, even brands you’ve used before. Full dairy-free and gluten-free swaps, with my favorite brands, are in the post above.
  • Dairy-Free: Use dairy-free butter (sticks or blocks, not tub), dairy-free sour cream or yogurt, non-dairy heavy cream for the glaze, and dairy-free chocolate chips.
  • Gluten-Free: Use a gluten-free all-purpose flour blend made for baking. If your blend doesn’t contain xanthan gum, add ¼ teaspoon per cup (140 g) of flour.
 
Recipe Tips:
  • Grease every groove: A missed spot is the most common reason a Bundt cake sticks. See the full troubleshooting guide in the post above.
  • Use mini chips: They stay spread through the thick batter instead of sinking.
  • Give it time:     This is a big, moist cake that needs the full 60 to 70 minutes. Don’t pull it early.
 
I appreciate your feedback, and it helps others, too! Recipe reviews on the website are extremely valuable to other readers online. So, please don’t forget to give it a 5-star rating below.
